# Air receiver -- TIA Portal starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The function block's body is yours.*

**The task.** While the station runs, keep the receiver between the pot less 0.5 bar and the pot: open receiver.supply at the bottom of the band, close it at the top. receiver.pressure is the card's raw count -- 0 at 4 mA, 27648 at 20 mA, over 0..10 bar -- so scale it (NORM_X, then SCALE_X) and show bar on the gauge. Open the isolation valve while the station runs and prove it by valve.opened: it takes 2 s to travel, and if it has not arrived when that and a margin have run out, it has failed -- alarm, and stop.

**Done when.** The needle on the receiver's own gauge and the one you drive agree, and the receiver cycles inside the band -- still after the plant draws harder (the receiver's Consumption) and after you move the pot. Divide by 32767 instead of 27648 and everything reads 16 % low and the receiver runs 16 % high. Seize the valve (valve.fault) and Start: valve.opened never comes, and only a timer on the feedback notices -- but a check without one alarms on every healthy start, because for two seconds neither limit switch is made.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`air_receiver.scl`](air_receiver.scl) | SCL source: the global DB `FF_IO` with every signal, and an empty FB `"AirReceiver"`. |
| [`opcua_mapping.json`](opcua_mapping.json) | For `--driver opcua-client`: tag id -> `ns=3;s="FF_IO"."..."`. |
| [`snap7_mapping.json`](snap7_mapping.json) | For `--driver s7-snap7`: tag id -> `DBX`/`DBD` offset in `FF_IO`. |
| [`plcsim_mapping.json`](plcsim_mapping.json) | For `--driver plcsim-advanced`: tag id -> `FF_IO.<Name>`. |

The Siemens walkthrough -- PLCSIM Advanced, the OPC UA server, finding
NodeIds -- is [`../README.md`](../README.md). This page is only what is
different about this scene.

## Set it up

1. In a project with an S7-1500 CPU: *External source files -> Add new
   external file*, pick `air_receiver.scl`, then right-click it -> *Generate
   blocks from source*. That creates `FF_IO` and `"AirReceiver"`. One
   exercise per CPU: this `FF_IO` replaces any other one.
2. Call `"AirReceiver"` from OB1 (drag it into `Main`; TIA creates the
   instance DB).
3. Check `FF_IO`'s properties: *Optimized block access* off (the source sets
   it), *Accessible from HMI/OPC UA* and *Writable from HMI/OPC UA* on for
   every member (TIA's default). Without *Writable* every sensor reads FALSE
   forever.
4. Compile, download, RUN.

## Run it

Open the scene in FactoryForge first (pick "Air receiver" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/air_receiver.json)), then attach
the sidecar with whichever driver reaches your CPU, in the folder
FactoryForge was extracted to:

```
.\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver opcua-client --mapping examples/tia/air-receiver/opcua_mapping.json -o url opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840
.\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver s7-snap7 -o host <cpu-ip> -o db <FF_IO's number> --mapping examples/tia/air-receiver/snap7_mapping.json
.\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver plcsim-advanced -o instance <name> --mapping examples/tia/air-receiver/plcsim_mapping.json
```

On Linux it is `./factoryforge-sidecar`. To have it marked, stop the sidecar and
start the grader in place of the 3D scene, in one terminal:

```
.\factoryforge-sidecar grade --scene air-receiver
```

then run the same `connect` command in a second terminal with the bus port
the grader printed added: `--port <bus port it printed>`.

<!-- from-source -->
(From a source checkout: `python -m factoryforge_sidecar` in place of
`.\factoryforge-sidecar`, with the sidecar installed and run from the repository
root so the paths resolve.)
<!-- /from-source -->

The OPC UA namespace index is usually 3, not always: run
`.\factoryforge-sidecar browse opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840` once and fix `ns=` in
the mapping if yours differs.

## FF_IO

In declaration order. `PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp);
`PLC reads` is an input (a sensor, a button, a measurement). The two
directions never share a byte, so the snap7 driver never rewrites a bit your
program owns. `FF_IO` is 16 bytes. *Brief* marks the signals the task
names.

| Tag | Direction | Member | Type | Offset | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pressure_gauge.value` | PLC writes | `PressureGaugeValue` | Real | DBD0 | needle position, scale 0..10 bar | yes |
| `alarm.beacon` | PLC writes | `AlarmBeacon` | Bool | DBX4.0 | rotating alarm beacon | yes |
| `alarm.horn` | PLC writes | `AlarmHorn` | Bool | DBX4.1 | alarm horn | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | `PanelGreen` | Bool | DBX4.2 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | `PanelRed` | Bool | DBX4.3 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `receiver.supply` | PLC writes | `ReceiverSupply` | Bool | DBX4.4 | open the receiver's supply valve (load the receiver) | yes |
| `valve.open` | PLC writes | `ValveOpen` | Bool | DBX4.5 | energise the solenoid: the valve travels open (spring closes it when dropped) | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | `PanelSetpoint` | Real | DBD6 | the operator's pot, 4..6.5 bar (starts at 6) | yes |
| `receiver.pressure` | PLC reads | `ReceiverPressure` | DInt | DBD10 | receiver pressure, RAW counts: 0 = 0 bar, 27648 = 10 bar, 32767 = wire break | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | `PanelEstop` | Bool | DBX14.0 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | `PanelReset` | Bool | DBX14.1 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | `PanelStart` | Bool | DBX14.2 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | `PanelStop` | Bool | DBX14.3 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `receiver.wirebreak` | PLC reads | `ReceiverWirebreak` | Bool | DBX14.4 | the card's wire-break diagnostic for the 4-20 mA loop | yes |
| `valve.closed` | PLC reads | `ValveClosed` | Bool | DBX14.5 | limit switch: valve fully closed; mid-travel neither is made (2 s end to end) | yes |
| `valve.fault` | PLC reads | `ValveFault` | Bool | DBX14.6 | TRUE = the stem has seized; the feedback no longer follows the command | yes |
| `valve.opened` | PLC reads | `ValveOpened` | Bool | DBX14.7 | limit switch: valve fully open | yes |

`int` travels as a `DInt` and `float` as a `Real`: the OPC UA driver writes
Int32 and Float, and a member of any other type is refused as a type mismatch.
Hold anything the scene must see for well over a second on OPC UA: an
S7-1500 forces a 1000 ms publishing interval on subscriptions, which is why the
driver polls by default.
